description: How the browser reaches the session (plugin/bin/.thimble-watch): the watcher wakes the session with each browser event, and permission prompts are relayed to the browser. As each turn of main's begins and ends, the permission mode Claude Code reports for it goes to the server, which the sessions thimble starts follow by default. The turn that ends after /thimble shows the dashboard link in the terminal, where the model does not see it. As each turn of main's begins, the events held for main (an ended orientation, writer or view build, a label) are added to its prompt, and the terminal prints what the analyst wrote in the browser, which Claude Code shows of a woken turn only as the fixed summary. The start and end of each run of thimble's orientation, critic and writers print a line after a tool call or a prompt, main's Agent call that would start a second tray entry of an agent or a second fork of a thread is refused, and an agent's tray entry is kept going while the agent runs. In a session that is no thimble workspace, each exits at once. The UserPromptExpansion hook of /thimble does the skill's work (bin/thimble server up --hook) just before the skill's commands run, since Claude Code runs hooks outside its Bash sandbox, where a command cannot start or reach thimble's server; the skill's command prints what it left. The SessionStart hook for clear and compact gives main its prompt again (bin/thimble prompt main), which /clear takes out of the conversation and /compact cuts short in a session the launcher did not start; it prints nothing in any other session.

hooks.command: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/thimble" prompt main --unless-launched --if-main --cwd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" --lead 'Your thimble prompt follows. /thimble gave it to you, and /clear or /compact has since taken it out of this conversation or cut it short. It is yours for the rest of this session, as if it were part of your system prompt. When Claude Code shows only the start of it and names a file that holds all of it, Read that file before you reply to anything.' 2>/dev/null || true
